newsitem.title: USA: Away on Business: An Internet guidebook.
newsitem.headline: Away on Business: An Internet guidebook.

text.p: The landslide of Internet information available to business travelers grows and changes so quickly there are few ways to keep track of it.
Even for those travelers who can't book their own airline and hotel reservations directly online because of corporate policy, there is still an amazing amount of road-friendly data to be tapped.
A good chunk of it has now been corralled in a book, "Net Travel: How Travelers Use the Internet" (O'Reilly, $24.95 paperback) by Michael Shapiro, a San Francisco-area writer.

--Subway maps for 60 systems in 29 countries are available at http://metro.jussieu.fr:10001/bin/cities/english. Locate an airport stop on a subway system, for example, plug in a destination and the site spits out a station-by-station route with changes of train as needed.

-- Want to read a little about the town you're about to visit? Try the local newspaper. Links to hundreds of newspaper sites in the United States and beyond may be found at http://www.newspapers.com. It includes a point-and-click map. There are business journals and other publications listed by town, and the breadth of daily journalism available online ranges from big city to small town.

-- Travelers thinking about extending their stay on a weekend when a business trip is finished might find hotel bargains at http://www.travelweb.com. Hyatt and Sheraton are among the hotels posting cut-rate weekend prices.

-- Restaurant information, including menus and prices in some cases, is widely available by city. Shapiro suggests using a Web search tool such as Yahoo! to look for city information and go from there.
The book also explains how airline booking sites operate and who runs them. The book is available at retail stores across the United States. Information can also be obtained at 1-800-998-9938.

Travel guru Arthur Frommer, in an introduction to the book, says it provides "an important service to both the travel industry and the traveling public ... it is well researched, thorough and imaginatively presented."
Frommer's travel site, the "Outspoken Encyclopedia of Travel," can be found at http://www.frommer.com.

Business travelers: Question, complaint or pet peeve? Send them to Away on Business, c/o Reuters, Room 1170, 311 S. Wacker Dr., Chicago 60606. Or via Internet E-mail Mike.Conlon(at)Reuters.com using the "at" sign on computer keyboards. We cannot promise personal replies but will try to address letters as space permits.
